facts.fact: Google's release notes dated 2026-04-22 rename Vertex AI to Agent Platform, part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Vertex AI Studio was renamed Agent Studio per release notes dated 2026-04-22 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Vertex AI Search was renamed Agent Search per release notes dated 2026-04-22 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Vertex AI RAG Engine was renamed RAG Engine within Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform per release notes dated 2026-04-22 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Vertex AI Agent Engine was renamed Agent Runtime per release notes dated 2026-04-22 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
The release notes say 'Agent Builder is now part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
After the rename to Agent Platform, IAM role IDs keep the `roles/aiplatform.*` and `roles/discoveryengine.*` prefixes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Google Cloud docs moved to docs.cloud.google.com: `https://cloud.google.com/docs`, `https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs` and `https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs` return 301 redirects to `https://docs.cloud.google.com/...` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs)

The Agent Platform docs root is `https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform`, organised into Build, Scale, Govern and Optimize (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform)

The Google Cloud resource hierarchy runs Organization (root), optional nestable Folders, Projects, then service resources; every resource except the root has exactly one parent, and allow, deny and organization policies set at the organization or a folder are inherited by all descendants (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

An Organization resource requires Google Workspace or Cloud Identity; each account links to exactly one organization, which is provisioned automatically when a user in that account creates a project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)
A Google Workspace account can back the Google Cloud Organization resource (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)
The organization's initial allow policy grants Project Creator and Billing Account Creator to the whole domain (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

The Workspace or Cloud Identity super admin verifies the domain and assigns the Google Cloud Organization Administrator role (`roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin`) to the people who then administer IAM across the hierarchy (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

The project ID is chosen at creation and used in most requests, while the auto-generated read-only project number is what service agent emails and federation principal identifiers use (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)

Google Cloud Setup offers three foundation tiers: 'Proof of concept' (organization, billing and hierarchy), 'Production' (adds logging, monitoring and Security Command Center) and 'Advanced production' (adds networking and Cloud KMS with Autokey) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/enterprise/setup-checklist)

Billing account roles are `roles/billing.admin` (Billing Account Administrator), `roles/billing.user` (Billing Account User, links projects), `roles/billing.viewer`, `roles/billing.projectManager` (Project Billing Manager) and `roles/billing.creator` (Billing Account Creator, granted at the organization) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/billing-access)

Linking a project to billing needs `roles/billing.user` on the billing account plus `roles/billing.projectManager` or Owner on the project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/billing-access)
Linking a project to a billing account needs Project Billing Manager (`roles/billing.projectManager`) or Owner on the project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/billing-access)

Accepting a Marketplace private offer needs `roles/billing.admin`, or `roles/billing.user` plus `roles/consumerprocurement.orderAdmin`, on the Cloud Billing account named in the offer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/marketplace/docs/offers/accepting-private-offer)
With `roles/billing.user`, `roles/consumerprocurement.orderAdmin` allows accepting a private offer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/marketplace/docs/offers/accepting-private-offer)
A Marketplace private offer can be accepted only once (https://docs.cloud.google.com/marketplace/docs/offers/accepting-private-offer)
Partner models in Model Garden, for example Anthropic Claude, need a procurement entitlement (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)

An admin with Consumer Procurement Entitlement Manager (`roles/consumerprocurement.entitlementManager`) enables a partner model in Model Garden (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)

The Cloud Commerce Consumer Procurement API (`cloudcommerceconsumerprocurement.googleapis.com`) must be allowed for partner models if service usage is restricted (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)

Agent Platform express mode is a trial path open to @gmail.com Google Accounts without full project setup, with a 90-day limit and only basic generative AI services (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/start/express-mode/overview)

Express mode authenticates with an API key against the global `aiplatform.googleapis.com` endpoint, whose paths have no project or location segment (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/start/express-mode/overview)

facts.fact: What to ask the client for on day one (synthesised from Google's setup and access-control pages): an org-domain or federated user identity; a project (with its ID and number) under the right folder, linked to a billing account; the APIs enabled (e.g. `aiplatform.googleapis.com`); `roles/aiplatform.user` on the project; `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the runtime service account; the region and endpoint policy (regional, `us`/`eu` multi-region, or global); the VPC-SC perimeter membership; any `vertexai.allowedModels` restrictions; and partner-model enablement if needed (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/control-model-access)
Enabling APIs such as `aiplatform.googleapis.com` needs `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)
Day-one Agent Platform access needs `roles/aiplatform.user` on the project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)
Day-one Agent Platform access needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the runtime service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

Ask the client on day one for any `vertexai.allowedModels` restrictions and VPC-SC perimeter membership affecting Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/control-model-access)

Cloud Identity and Google Workspace support SAML 2.0 SSO with Google as the service provider, via SAML profiles (multiple IdPs) or the legacy single-IdP profile (https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/single-sign-on)
IdP-initiated sign-on is not supported for Cloud Identity or Workspace SAML SSO (https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/single-sign-on)
Super admins can bypass SSO, so their MFA must be set up in Google directly (https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/single-sign-on)

Workforce Identity Federation lets users from any OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP (Entra ID, AD FS, Okta) sign in without being copied into Cloud Identity; workforce pools are configured at the organization level (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)
Workforce principals look like `principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL_ID/subject/SUBJECT` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)
Workforce Identity Federation token exchange defaults to 1,000 requests per minute per organization (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)

SCIM for Workforce Identity Federation was announced at Next '26; Google's IAM blog of 2026-05-06 lists it without stating a status (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)

2-step verification is enforced for sign-in to the Google Cloud console and the Firebase console, not for the gcloud CLI or data-plane traffic (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/mfa-requirement)

2SV enforcement dates: personal accounts on or after 2025-05-12; non-SSO Cloud Identity organizations created before 2026-08-03 on or after 2026-10-20; organizations created on or after 2026-08-03 30 days after creation; federated/SSO users 'To be announced' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/mfa-requirement)

Google Cloud has three service account types: user-managed (created by you), default (created when some services are enabled, e.g. `PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`) and Google-managed service agents (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-overview)
Attaching a service account to a resource needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-overview)
Managing a service account needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-overview)

A principal with `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` gets short-lived tokens for a service account; audit logs typically record both the caller and the service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-impersonation)
`iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` is in Service Account Token Creator (`roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-impersonation)
In gcloud, impersonate a service account with `--impersonate-service-account` or the `impersonate-service-account` property (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-impersonation)

Service account access tokens default to a maximum of 1 hour (3,600 s) and can be extended to 12 hours (43,200 s) by listing the service account in `constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension`; ID tokens last 1 hour (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/create-short-lived-credentials-direct)

Organizations created on or after 2024-05-03 enforce by default `constraints/iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`, `constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload`, `constraints/iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts` (stops default service accounts getting Editor), `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` (domain-restricted sharing) and `constraints/storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/secure-by-default-organizations)
Secure-by-default organizations block service account key creation and upload, so plan for keyless authentication (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/secure-by-default-organizations)

facts.fact: Workload Identity Federation (keyless) supports AWS, Azure/Entra ID, GitHub, GitLab, Terraform, Kubernetes, Okta, X.509, AD FS and any OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP, and its pieces are workload identity pools (one per environment recommended), providers, STS token exchange per RFC 8693, CEL attribute mappings and attribute conditions (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)
Workload Identity Federation exchanges tokens through Security Token Service per RFC 8693 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)
Federation CEL attribute mappings require `google.subject` (max 127 characters) and allow up to 50 custom attributes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)

Federated principal identifiers use the project number, not the project ID: a single subject is `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL_ID/subject/SUBJECT`, and groups and attributes use `principalSet://.../group/GROUP_ID` and `principalSet://.../attribute.NAME/VALUE` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)

Direct resource access grants roles straight to the `principal://` or `principalSet://` identifier and is Google's recommendation, though some APIs have limitations (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)
The service account impersonation method grants the federated principal `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` on a service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)

GitHub Actions federation uses issuer `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/` with minimum mapping `google.subject=assertion.sub`, and the job needs `permissions: id-token: write` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)

An attribute condition is required for GitHub federation because GitHub shares one issuer across all orgs, for example `assertion.repository_owner=='ORG'`; Google recommends the numeric `repository_id` and `repository_owner_id` claims (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)
Creating workload identity pools needs `roles/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)

The `google-github-actions/auth` action is at v3 and lists three options in order of preference: direct Workload Identity Federation, federation through a service account, and service account key JSON (https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth)

With `google-github-actions/auth`, direct federation tokens last at most 10 minutes, not all resources accept `principalSet`, and minting OAuth access or ID tokens requires the service-account path (https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth)

For AWS federation, create the provider with `create-aws` and the 12-digit account ID, map `google.subject=assertion.arn` plus `attribute.aws_role=assertion.arn.extract('assumed-role/{role_name}/')`, and use the condition `assertion.arn.startsWith('arn:aws:sts::AWS_ACCOUNT_ID:assumed-role/')` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-other-clouds)

Add `--enable-imdsv2` to `gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred-config ... --aws` for IMDSv2 instances, and use `create-cred-config ... --azure --app-id-uri` to generate an Azure credential file (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-other-clouds)

For Azure federation, create an OIDC provider with issuer `https://sts.windows.net/TENANT_ID` and allowed audience set to the Entra app's Application ID URI (for example `api://my-app`), and map `google.subject=assertion.sub`; for a managed identity the `sub` is its Object ID (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-other-clouds)

Each agent gets a SPIFFE-based identity `spiffe://TRUST_DOMAIN/resources/SERVICE/RESOURCE_PATH`, used in IAM as `principal://TRUST_DOMAIN/...`, with trust domain `agents.global.org-ORGANIZATION_ID.system.id.goog` (or `agents.global.proj-PROJECT_NUMBER.system.id.goog` without an organization) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/agent-identity-overview)

An Agent Identity X.509 certificate is auto-provisioned, valid 24 hours and renewed automatically; Agent Identity is supported on Agent Runtime, Gemini Enterprise, Cloud Run and GKE (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/agent-identity-overview)

Release notes say Agent Identity reached GA on 2026-04-22; Google's IAM blog of 2026-05-06 lists Agent Identity for Agent Runtime and IAM Allow and Deny policies for Agent Identity as GA, and Agent Identity for Agent Platform, Agent Identity Auth Manager, Principal Access Boundary for Agent Identity, and VPC-SC ingress and egress rules for Agent Identity as Preview (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes ; https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)
Agent Identity for Agent Runtime is GA per Google's IAM blog of 2026-05-06 (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)
The Agent Identity API (`agentidentity.googleapis.com`) entered Preview on 2026-06-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Agent Identity Auth Manager is Preview per Google's IAM blog of 2026-05-06 (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)

Agent Identity principal formats for Agent Runtime: one agent `principal://agents.global.org-ORG_ID.system.id.goog/resources/aiplatform/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/LOCATION/reasoningEngines/ENGINE_ID`; all agents in a project `principalSet://agents.global.org-ORG_ID.system.id.goog/attribute.platformContainer/aiplatform/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER`; all agents in an org `principalSet://agents.global.org-ORG_ID.system.id.goog/*` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)

facts.fact: Agent Identity tokens are certificate-bound by default: a Google-managed Context-Aware Access policy binds tokens to the agent's certificate, enforcing DPoP and mTLS, and ID tokens carry a `cnf` (`x5t#S256`) claim (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)

To call a plain `*.run.app` URL with Agent Identity, opt out of token binding per request with `bind_id_token=False`, available in `google-auth` 2.61.0 on GKE and 2.62.0 on Cloud Run (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)
`GOOGLE_API_ENABLE_RUNTIME_BOUND_TOKEN=false` turns token binding off across the runtime and is discouraged (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)

Enable Agent Identity on an Agent Runtime agent by setting `identity_type` to `AGENT_IDENTITY` via `types.IdentityType.AGENT_IDENTITY` in the Python SDK, `agents-cli deploy --agent-identity`, or the ADK `.agent_engine_config.json`; instances without the flag keep using service accounts, and `effectiveIdentity` shows which identity is in use (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity)
`agents-cli deploy --agent-identity` deploys an Agent Runtime agent with Agent Identity (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity)
The ADK `.agent_engine_config.json` can set `identity_type` to `AGENT_IDENTITY` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity)

Agent Identity Auth Manager is a credential vault and broker for API keys, OAuth client credentials and delegated end-user OAuth tokens; it handles user sign-in, consent and revocation and attributes end-user access events to the agent's SPIFFE ID (Preview per the 2026-05-06 IAM blog) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/agent-identity-overview ; https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)

Google Cloud IAM grants roles (bundles of permissions) to principals on resources through allow policies; effective access is the union of a resource's and its ancestors' policies, deny policies block permissions even when a role grants them, Principal Access Boundary policies limit which resources a principal is eligible to access, and IAM Conditions add attribute-based logic (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/overview)
IAM role types are basic (Owner/Editor/Viewer, not recommended in production), predefined and custom (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/overview)

`roles/aiplatform.admin` gives full Agent Platform access; the core roles also include `roles/aiplatform.editor` and `roles/aiplatform.viewer` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)

`roles/aiplatform.user`, titled 'Agent Platform User', gives use access to most resources and includes `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/aiplatform)

Agent-specific Agent Platform roles are all Beta: `roles/aiplatform.agentsAdmin` covers agents, their memories and access control policies; `roles/aiplatform.agentsCreator` creates and discovers agents and auth providers; `roles/aiplatform.agentsUser` views agents and manages their tasks; `roles/aiplatform.agentsViewer` is read-only (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)
Memory Bank roles are `roles/aiplatform.memoryEditor`, `roles/aiplatform.memoryUser` and `roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)
Sessions roles are `roles/aiplatform.sessionEditor`, `roles/aiplatform.sessionUser` and `roles/aiplatform.sessionViewer` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)
`roles/aiplatform.expressUser` and `roles/aiplatform.expressAdmin` (Beta) cover express mode (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)

`roles/aiplatform.provisionedThroughputAdmin` (Beta) creates, views, updates and cancels Provisioned Throughput orders (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/provisioned-throughput/purchase-provisioned-throughput)
Deploying to Agent Runtime needs `roles/aiplatform.user` on the project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

Deploying to Agent Runtime from an agent object needs `roles/storage.admin` on the staging bucket; source-file deploys need no bucket (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)
Deploying to Agent Runtime with a custom runtime service account needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on it (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)
Enabling the APIs for Agent Runtime needs `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

Agent Runtime's default identity is the Reasoning Engine service agent `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform-re.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with `roles/aiplatform.reasoningEngineServiceAgent`, which carries the default permissions deployed agents need; add roles to it if the agent needs more (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

Reading Secret Manager secrets from an Agent Runtime agent needs `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/manage-agent-access)

facts.fact: A custom service account for Agent Runtime 'likely needs' `roles/aiplatform.user` plus whatever the agent code requires (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

For an Agent Runtime service account in another project, `iam.disableCrossProjectServiceAccountUsage` must not be enforced in the account's project, and the Agent Platform Service Agent needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` in that project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

The Agent Platform Service Agent needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` in the project of a cross-project Agent Runtime service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime/setup)

Agent identities get `roles/aiplatform.agentDefaultAccess` and `roles/aiplatform.agentContextEditor` by default; recommended extras are `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer`, `roles/browser`, `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` and `roles/storage.objectViewer`, and the docs advise against project-level `roles/aiplatform.user` for agent identities (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)
Agent-to-agent calls need `roles/agentregistry.viewer`, plus `roles/aiplatform.user` on the target reasoning engine (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)

Deleting an agent leaves its IAM bindings in place, so remove them manually; a redeployed agent with a new resource ID is a new principal and needs fresh grants; agent identities cannot hold legacy Cloud Storage bucket roles such as `storage.legacyBucketReader` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/agent-identity-overview)

Agent Platform service agents: Agent Platform (AI Platform) Service Agent `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`roles/aiplatform.serviceAgent`); RAG Data Service Agent `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-vertex-rag.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`roles/aiplatform.ragServiceAgent`); Custom Code Service Agent `@gcp-sa-aiplatform-cc` (`roles/aiplatform.customCodeServiceAgent`); Reasoning Engine `@gcp-sa-aiplatform-re` (`roles/aiplatform.reasoningEngineServiceAgent`); Fine Tuning `@gcp-sa-aiplatform-ft`; Rapid Eval `@gcp-sa-vertex-eval`; Memory Bank `@gcp-sa-vertex-memory` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)

The Agent Platform (AI Platform) Service Agent is `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with role `roles/aiplatform.serviceAgent` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents)
Agent Platform service agents are created on first use, or explicitly with `gcloud beta services identity create` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)

To use data in another project (BigQuery, Cloud Storage), grant the service agent roles there (in the console, tick 'Include Google-provided role grants'); don't remove default service agent roles, and never grant service agent roles to humans (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control)

The Discovery Engine service agent for Agent Search / Gemini Enterprise is `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-discoveryengine.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with role `roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents)

Other agent-relevant service agents: Cloud Run `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@serverless-robot-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`roles/run.serviceAgent`), Apigee `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-apigee.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`roles/apigee.serviceAgent`), BigQuery Connection `@gcp-sa-bigqueryconnection` (`roles/bigqueryconnection.serviceAgent`) and Agent Gateway `@gcp-sa-agentgateway` (`roles/agentgateway.serviceAgent`) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents)

Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) roles keep the Discovery Engine names `roles/discoveryengine.admin`, `roles/discoveryengine.editor`, `roles/discoveryengine.user` and `roles/discoveryengine.viewer`; `roles/monitoring.viewer` may also be needed to see app monitoring (https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/access-control)

Typical least-privilege BigQuery access for agent runtime identities pairs `roles/bigquery.jobUser` (run queries; project, folder or org level only) with `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` on specific datasets (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control)

Agent runtime identities reading BigQuery data need `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` on specific datasets; broader roles are `roles/bigquery.user`, `roles/bigquery.dataEditor`, `roles/bigquery.dataOwner` and `roles/bigquery.admin`, and related roles are `roles/bigquery.readSessionUser` (Storage Read API) and `roles/bigquery.connectionUser` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control)

Cloud Run roles are `roles/run.admin`, `roles/run.developer`, `roles/run.viewer`, `roles/run.invoker`, `roles/run.servicesInvoker`, `roles/run.jobsExecutor` and `roles/run.sourceDeveloper` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles)
Deploying to Cloud Run needs `roles/run.developer` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles)
Deploying to Cloud Run needs `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` (`iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`) on the runtime service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles)
Deploying to Cloud Run needs `roles/artifactregistry.reader` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles)
The Cloud Run runtime defaults to the Compute Engine default service account; Google recommends a dedicated user-managed one (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles)

facts.fact: Apigee roles are `roles/apigee.admin` (Org Admin), `roles/apigee.apiAdminV2`, `roles/apigee.developerAdmin`, `roles/apigee.environmentAdmin`, `roles/apigee.analyticsViewer` and `roles/apigee.readOnlyAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/apigee-roles)
`roles/apigee.admin` (Org Admin) is the only Apigee role that can create or delete organizations (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/apigee-roles)

On the client side, Organization Administrator (`roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin`) or folder admins grant inherited roles (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

Project IAM Admin (`roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin`) and Security Admin (`roles/iam.securityAdmin`) grant roles on target resources, including to agent identities (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)
Security Admin (`roles/iam.securityAdmin`) can grant roles on target resources, including to agent identities (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/auth-agent-own-identity)
Billing Account Administrator handles billing links and Marketplace on the client side (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/billing-access)

An Organization Policy Administrator sets constraints such as `vertexai.allowedModels`; this is the standard Org Policy role, which the Agent Platform page does not name (https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

The org policy `vertexai.allowedModels` takes entries `publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL:ACTION` with ACTION `predict`, `deploy` or `tune` (for example `publishers/google/models/gemini-3.5-flash:predict`) and can be set at organization, folder or project level, where an explicit deny overrides an allow (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/control-model-access)
`vertexai.allowedModels` has no wildcards and at most 500 values (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/control-model-access)

IAM Unified Access Policies (UAP, IAM v3 'Access policies') govern agent traffic through Agent Gateway with allow or deny rules (deny overrides allow) on agent principals and CEL conditions such as tool name, HTTP method or path prefix, bound to the project that holds the gateway (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/policies/iam-overview-uap)
Unified Access Policies are enforced by IAP in `DRY_RUN` (audit-only) or `ENFORCE` mode (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/policies/iam-overview-uap)
Release notes give Unified Access Policies as GA on 2026-08-31; the 2026-05-06 blog had said 'coming soon' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Agent Platform training restriction: 'Google won't use your data to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models without your prior permission or instruction', applying to GA and pre-GA managed models, set out in the Service Specific Terms with processing covered by the Cloud Data Processing Addendum (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance ; https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms)

Implicit caching for Gemini is on by default; in-memory and durable caches are project-scoped and deleted within 24 hours, and the durable cache does not support CMEK (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)

A principal with `roles/aiplatform.admin` can turn off durable caching or all caching per project; organization-wide changes go through the account team (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)

Google may log prompts to detect Acceptable Use Policy abuse; zero data retention requires request-response logging left off, `store = false` on the Interactions API (default `true`), caching disabled, no Live API session resumption and no Sandbox Snapshot API (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)
The Interactions API defaults to `store = true`; set `store = false` for zero data retention (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)
Deep Research session data is kept for 7 days and cannot be disabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)

Grounding with Google Search keeps query logs up to 3 days with no opt-out, and Grounding with Google Search and Google Maps supports none of data residency, CMEK, VPC-SC or Access Transparency (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/security-controls)
For zero data retention Google points to Web Grounding for Enterprise instead of Grounding with Google Search (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/data-governance)

Gemini data at rest stays in the customer-selected location; `us`/`eu` multi-region endpoints (`aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com`; EU excludes UK and Switzerland) keep ML processing inside that jurisdiction, single-region endpoints keep it inside the broader country or multi-region jurisdiction (varying by model), and the `global` endpoint gives 'no regional isolation or data residency guarantees' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/locations)

facts.fact: The org policy `constraints/gcp.restrictEndpointUsage` can block global endpoint requests (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)
Multi-region `.rep.` endpoints do not support Private Google Access, so use Private Service Connect instead (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/locations)

The Agent Platform security-controls matrix is per model: GA Gemini models list data residency, CMEK, VPC-SC and Access Transparency for online and batch inference, context caching lacks CMEK, and 'Security controls are not supported for preview models.' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/security-controls)
RAG Engine supports CMEK and VPC-SC but not data residency or Access Transparency (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/security-controls)

VPC Service Controls perimeters block API access across the boundary and are refined by Access Context Manager access levels, ingress and egress rules (preferred over bridges), and dry-run mode (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview)

`restricted.googleapis.com` resolves to 199.36.153.4/30; an organization has one org-level access policy, and scoped policies delegate perimeter administration to folders or projects (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview)

The VPC-SC perimeter covers Agent Platform Gemini generative AI, online and batch inference, tuning, Vector Search, Pipelines, Colab Enterprise, Agent Runtime and sandboxes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vpc-service-controls)

Under VPC-SC, Agent Runtime agents deployed before the project joined the perimeter are not protected, Agent Runtime has no internet egress (needs a proxy in an RFC 1918 subnet plus Cloud NAT), endpoints must be created after joining the perimeter, and URL-context live fetching and request-response logging are unavailable (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vpc-service-controls)
Agent Gateway enforces VPC-SC perimeter rules with `ALL_TRAFFIC` egress mode for deployments created after 2026-09-08 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Computer Use and Shell sandboxes went GA with VPC-SC and Private Service Connect on 2026-09-09 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

VPC-SC support for Agent Identity ingress and egress rules was Preview per the 2026-05-06 blog (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)
CMEK covers Agent Runtime, sandboxes, endpoints, models, datasets, batch jobs, pipelines and Vector Search on Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/cmek)
For CMEK the Agent Platform Service Agent needs `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the key (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/cmek)

The CMEK key must be in the same region as the resource, not dual- or multi-region, except that serving profiles for the Gemini Live and Interactions APIs need `us`/`eu` keys (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/cmek)
CMEK for Gemini 3 tuning jobs and tuned models went GA on 2026-10-19 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

From 2026-11-06 Memory Bank instances can choose Google-managed or Cloud KMS encryption in the console; Memory Bank and Sessions do not support the global endpoint for CMEK (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/cmek)

Agent Gateway governs client-to-agent (ingress) and agent-to-anywhere (egress) traffic for Agent Runtime and Gemini Enterprise agents and is default-deny: 'all connections are blocked unless an explicit IAM policy grants access' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview)
Agent Gateway integrates IAP, Unified Access Policies, Model Armor and Agent Registry (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview)
Agent Gateway integrates Agent Registry, with up to 5,000 registered resources per gateway (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview)
Agent Gateway integrates IAP for enforcement of agent traffic policies (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview)
Agent Gateway integrates Unified Access Policies (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview)

Agent Gateway support for GKE and Cloud Run is 'coming soon', and cross-cloud support went to Limited Preview on 2026-11-11 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Model Armor screens prompts and responses for prompt injection and jailbreaks, sensitive data (via Sensitive Data Protection), malicious URLs (the first 256), RAI categories and CSAM, and floor settings enforce minimum protections across a project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/model-armor/overview)
Model Armor is billed on tokens screened (https://docs.cloud.google.com/model-armor/overview)

Google announced inline Model Armor for Agent Gateway, Agent Runtime and Google Cloud MCP servers at Next '26, with the Firebase integration GA (blog of 2026-05-06) (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/whats-new-in-iam-security-governance-and-runtime-defense/)

Admin Activity logs for `aiplatform.googleapis.com` are always on, while Data Access logs, which include `generateContent` and `predict` calls as 'data read', are off by default and must be enabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/audit-logging)
Reading Agent Platform Data Access logs in `_Default` needs Private Logs Viewer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/audit-logging)

facts.fact: In dry-run mode, disallowed agent communications under Agent Gateway and UAP are written to Cloud Audit Logs without being blocked (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/policies/iam-overview-uap)
Inference request metadata logging went GA on 2026-10-30 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Release notes of 2026-06-18 tie Memory Bank and Sessions residency to configuring the resource location constraint in organization policy (`gcp.resourceLocations`) (unverified: full wording truncated) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Sessions data residency is tied to the `gcp.resourceLocations` organization policy constraint per release notes of 2026-06-18 (unverified: full wording truncated) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Generative AI on Vertex AI and Vertex AI Search received FedRAMP High authorization, announced 2025-03-20 (https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/public-sector/vertex-ai-search-and-generative-ai-with-gemini-achieve-fedramp-high)

Agent Search lists FedRAMP, ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS, BSI C5:2020 and HIPAA (a BAA is required) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/compliance-security-controls)

Gemini on Agent Platform is billed per 1M input and output tokens, varying by model and endpoint type (global, regional or multi-region); the pricing pages https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing and https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/pricing rendered without readable rates on 2026-11-14, so no figures are quoted (https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing)

Standard PayGo is the per-token standard rate for Gemini on Agent Platform, and Tier 4 (above $50,000 per 30 days) was added 2026-09-10 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/deploy/consumption-options ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Priority PayGo is a per-token premium rate with a ramp limit (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/deploy/consumption-options)
Flex PayGo is about 50% cheaper and latency-tolerant (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/deploy/consumption-options)
Batch inference is 50% cheaper than Standard (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/deploy/consumption-options)

Provisioned Throughput is bought in GSUs (generative AI scale units) on 1-week (Google models only), 1-month, 3-month or 1-year terms; fees can't be cancelled mid-term, auto-renewal applies to monthly and longer terms, and a 1-year term is priced 26% below the 1-month term (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/provisioned-throughput/purchase-provisioned-throughput)
Provisioned Throughput overage spills to Standard PayGo by default and can be controlled per request (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/deploy/consumption-options)
Ordering Provisioned Throughput needs `roles/aiplatform.provisionedThroughputAdmin` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/provisioned-throughput/purchase-provisioned-throughput)
Gemini 4 Hydrogen went GA on 2026-11-12 at 685 tokens/sec per GSU of Provisioned Throughput (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Gemini 4 Hydrogen cache writes are billed at 1.25x the input price from 2027-01-12 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
Provisioned Throughput for supervised fine-tuned models went GA on 2026-11-04 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Agent Runtime is billed on vCPU-hours and GiB-hours of memory; Session and Memory Bank compute has been metered on the Agent Platform compute SKU since 2026-09-01, and Memory Bank embedding SKUs are changing (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)

Third-party summaries quote roughly $0.085 per vCPU-hour and $0.009 per GiB-hour for Agent Runtime under the 2026 SKU consolidation; Google's pricing page did not render to confirm (secondary) (https://ecorpit.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform-cost-breakdown-2026/)

Partner models from Model Garden, such as Claude, are enabled through the Cloud Commerce Consumer Procurement entitlement and billed through Google Cloud pay-as-you-go per request or through Provisioned Throughput ('contact sales'), with pricing that varies by endpoint type (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)
Claude is a partner model from Model Garden billed through Google Cloud (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/partner-models/use-partner-models)

Agent Gateway cross-cloud is free during Limited Preview, while products configured with it (Model Armor, Cloud Logging, Cloud Trace) are billed at standard rates (release note of 2026-11-11) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes)
